headline: Redemption freeze likely driven by soured property deals and equity holdings requiring write-downs as higher cost of capital pressures DCF valuations
reasoning: Patrick William speculates that Metrics closing redemptions stems from two issues: exposure to property deals that have deteriorated, and equity holdings that cannot be held at par the way debt can. Unlike debt, where a loan can be held at 100 cents in the dollar as long as interest is being paid, equity valuations must stand on their own and are heavily impacted by discounted cash flow analysis. With the cost of capital having increased sharply over 12 months, even businesses with unchanged earnings profiles face significant valuation write-downs, forcing Metrics to take action.
quote: There may be a few things driving. That's the one is the property deals. The other, I suspect I speculate, is, you know, this audit report that's forced them to take write downs. And I suspect it's because metrics has got equity exposures. And the beauty of debt is, you know, you lend some $100. As long as they're paying interest, you can sort of hold it 100%. You can justify holding it at 100 cents a dollar. The problem with equity holdings is that equity valuation has to stand on its own, and one of the drivers of negative valuation is a discounted cash flow. So that cost of capital has skyrocketed over the last 12 months. So even if the business has the same earnings profile, if you're increasing your cost of capital by 2,030%. You're going to have to take it right down.
episode_title: The warning signs investors should watch in private credit

headline: Flagship ASX-listed vehicle: ~9 years old, 340 assets, weighted average term ~1.6 years, 60% hard real estate backing, net return has exceeded RBA cash rate by 4.4% minimum, fees compressed from 87bps to ~53-54bps
reasoning: The fund launched in October 2017 with a target of RBA cash rate plus 3.25% net, paid monthly. It has since outperformed that target, delivering at least 4.4% above the RBA cash rate on a net basis. The portfolio has grown from 55 initial loan assets to approximately 340 today, with average individual exposure of around 0.3% of 1%, providing high diversification. Management fees have been reduced from roughly 87 basis points to approximately 53-54 basis points. Around 60% of the book has hard real estate asset backing, and the weighted average term to maturity is approximately 1.6 years, limiting probability of default.
quote: We launched back in October of '17. The target in that fund was to deliver the RBA cash rate plus 3.25% net with income paid to investors each month. When we first launched the fund, it was diversified across 55 individual loan assets. Today, almost 9 years later, that fund has delivered a minimum net return over the RBA cash rate of 4.4%. We've also lowered the cost. So, the cost to the investor at the time we launched that fund was around about 87 basis points. It's now about 53, 54 basis points for memory. And and and then also we've diversified the asset holdings. So, it's gone from initially 55 assets to around about 340 assets today.
episode_title: Metrics Master Income Trust pt.1 - Fixed Interest Series

headline: Trading at a discount to NAV, implying early-to-mid teen returns on today's traded price versus 4.4% over RBA cash rate on NAV over 9-year period
reasoning: The speaker explains that MXT's listed vehicle trades at a discount to its daily-released NAV, and that discount is often driven by market information or general equity market concern rather than fundamental deterioration. Because the quoted yield and performance (4.4% over RBA cash rate over 9 years, net to investors) are calculated on NAV, buying at a discount to NAV amplifies the effective return to early-to-mid teen levels. The governance framework — independent responsible entity, independent third-party valuations, independent audit — is cited as giving investors confidence in the reliability of the NAV figure.
quote: So when a when the traded price then trades at a discount to that, that is really presenting a potential opportunity for an investor to say, 'Okay, well, I can acquire this asset today. I can if it trades back to the NAV cuz the the the the discount is often not because of fundamentals. It's often because of information in the market or general market equity market concern. It doesn't necessarily reflect that. But when we quote our returns and the yield, we're quoting it on a NAV. So the the performance of MX T when I said 4.4 over the RBA cash rate over a 9-year period net to investors when you actually then factor in the discount, it's it's generating sort of early to mid-teen returns for an investor based on today's traded price.
episode_title: Metrics Master Income Trust pt. 2 - Fixed Interest Series

headline: Highly diversified monthly income fund with long track record; active in workouts and restructures rather than forced selling
reasoning: The speaker describes Metrics Master Income Trust (MXT) as a highly diversified fund paying monthly income with attractive returns over a 13-year period. A key differentiator is the firm's willingness to engage in workouts and restructures rather than walking away or becoming a forced seller when credit situations deteriorate. The culture prioritises protecting investor capital and potentially profiting from distressed situations through active workout skills. The speaker acknowledges occasional media criticism but frames the approach as acting in investors' best interests.
quote: We have had to get involved in workouts or restructures, and we've got that skill set to be able to do that. And I think the benefit that we've delivered for our investors is we're not... it's not in our culture DNA to walk away from something. We won't sell it at a loss. We don't want to be put into a position where we're a forced seller. We believe that we're doing everything appropriately for the company in accordance with our obligations to shareholders, to our investors, but our primary objective is to make sure that we're delivering for our investors.
episode_title: Metrics Master Income Trust pt.3 - Fixed Interest Series
